questions.q: What makes a ServiceNow table different from a plain relational database table?
options: ServiceNow tables cannot store any real data
ServiceNow tables are only used for reporting, never for transactional records
The table itself is represented by a record in sys_db_object, and its columns are records in sys_dictionary
Tables in ServiceNow have no primary key of any kind
questions.explain: A ServiceNow table is metadata-driven: the table itself and each of its columns are rows you can query and edit, not a fixed schema file.

questions.q: Which table holds one record per table in the entire ServiceNow instance?
options: sys_dictionary
sys_db_object
sys_user
task
questions.explain: sys_db_object is the table of tables — System Definition > Tables is a list view built directly on it.

questions.q: What does a record in sys_dictionary represent?
options: A single user account
A single row of application data, like one incident
A single module in the Application Navigator
A single field (column) belonging to a specific table
questions.explain: Each column on a table is its own dictionary entry in sys_dictionary, pointing back at the table it belongs to.

options: A 32-character GUID that serves as the permanent, unique primary key auto-added to every table
A field that only exists on the Incident table
The display name shown for a record on a form
A setting that controls a user's time zone
questions.explain: sys_id is one of the standard fields ServiceNow auto-adds to every table, used as that record's permanent unique identifier.

questions.q: Why can an admin add a new field to the Incident table without writing a database migration script?
options: Incident is a special case that bypasses the dictionary entirely
New fields are only cosmetic and never stored anywhere
ServiceNow reads table and field structure live from sys_db_object and sys_dictionary, so adding a dictionary entry through the UI makes the field immediately available
Field changes require a full instance restart in every case
questions.explain: Because structure is metadata rather than a fixed schema, adding a sys_dictionary entry through the UI is enough — no DDL or restart needed.
